description: Journey — after each change: it also checks what the game chose (its scheme's gestures, fullscreen, right button, pointer capture, texts against the bindings). A playtest that passes is not a finished game: gripforge_game_audit (playtest="run" runs this test) gives the verdict and everything the tester cannot see. Play the project headless and report what works and what is broken. Run it after building or changing a game, before telling the user it is done. An automatic player spawns, walks, follows the mission waypoints, uses what offers a prompt, picks things up and attacks enemies. Probes check each capability the game provides (character control, combat, XP and levels, inventory, interactions, missions, needs, gathering, crafting, building, machines, world counters). Detectors flag a stuck player, unreachable goals, kit exceptions, NaN positions, a player under the ground, enemies that never reach the player, and step time. Then it checks the game on what it CHOSE, on a fresh run (lines game.*): the gestures its control scheme promises (a click game: click to walk, held to follow the cursor, click an enemy to strike, held to keep striking), fullscreen when the game offers it, the right button when the game gives it a role (no browser menu), the pointer captured exactly when the scheme looks with the mouse, and its texts (title, help, tutorial, dialogue) against the real bindings — never a fixed W A S D in a click game; nothing is imposed on a game that did not choose it. The frame rate is · not verified here: only a real page measures it (the play page reports it to the audit). Returns { summary, text, report, next }: text has one line per result, ✓ pass, ⚠ warning, ✕ failure, · not checked, each with its time, position, entity or kit; "provoked" means the tester set the condition up through the kit service. Fix the ✕ lines first, then run it again. report.notCovered lists the capabilities no probe looks at. report.replay replays the same inputs; pass it back as replay to check a fix against the same run. Deterministic: same project, seed and budget, same report. Runs in the compute service, about 5–20 s. 0 credits.

budget_seconds.description: Game time to play, in seconds (default 120).

project_id.description: Game Kit project id (gkp_…). Not a dedicated-server project (gpj_…) nor a Library item.

replay.description: report.replay of an earlier run: plays the same inputs again (seed and budget come from it).

seed.description: Seed of the run (default 1). The same seed gives the same report.

workspace_id.description: Workspace authorized by the current key. Never infer another user’s workspace.
